strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation: clearly articulates the structural mismatch between prompt-conditioned interface design and prompt-absent deployment scenarios, which extends broadly across automatic segmentation tasks
Elegant paradigm shift: from feature-space patching to prompt-space conditioning preserves the model's pre-trained geometric priors and aligns with SAM's original design philosophy
Asymmetric gating insight: PSG mechanism is well-justified for camouflaged scenes, with thoughtful residual anchoring design that acts as noise cancellation rather than feature reconstruction

Rigorous experimental validation: all baselines re-trained under identical conditions, comprehensive ablations (Tables 2-3) isolate contributions, cross-dataset medical segmentation transfer, 3-seed reporting with std
Excellent interpretability: Figure 4 provides compelling visualization of PSG mechanism showing precise suppressive boundaries; qualitative results clearly demonstrate ambiguity resolution
Parameter efficiency: achieves SOTA with only 21.26M trainable parameters, maintaining reasonable computational overhead (29 FPS vs 35 FPS for base SAM2)
Strong quantitative results: MAE 0.017 on COD10K, consistent improvements across multiple metrics (F_ω, Sm, E_φ) on four standard benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited component-level novelty: SPG uses standard TwoWayTransformer from SAM, PSG is conventional gating plus residual connection; core novelty lies in paradigm rather than algorithmic contributions

Unresolved critical failure mode: paper acknowledges that in extremely low-contrast scenarios SPG may fail to separate foreground/background, causing PSG to over-suppress targets; residual anchoring only 'partially alleviates' this issue without concrete solutions, directly undermining effectiveness for extreme camouflage

Strong dependency on foundation model capacity: performance degrades >8× (MAE 0.017→0.148) on smaller SAM2-T variant; limits practical deployment in resource-constrained settings with no proposed solutions

Continuous logit design lacks theoretical justification: feeding continuous masks to frozen prompt encoder designed for binary inputs is empirically effective but conceptually unconventional; explanation purely empirical without principled understanding

Incomplete hyperparameter ablation: loss weights fixed at λ_spg=λ_c=λ_r=1.0 without sensitivity analysis, Km=4 mask tokens appear arbitrary, batch size 1 raises stability concerns, no convergence analysis provided

Limited scope of generalization claims: medical evaluation only tests zero-shot transfer to similar tasks (polyp detection); no evaluation on fundamentally different segmentation tasks (scene, panoptic, instance) or other foundation models

Questionable oracle baseline: zero-shot SAM2 with GT point vs fine-tuned IP-SAM conflates foundation capacity, adaptation benefit, and paradigm contribution rather than isolating paradigm effectiveness

Incomplete baseline tuning: SAM2-AMG performs anomalously poorly (MAE 0.500 vs 0.182 null on CHAMELEON); no ablation on AMG configuration (top-1 selection strategy) raises questions about proper tuning
Inconsistent statistical reporting: standard deviations reported only for COD10K (±0.001), not for CAMO/CHAMELEON/NC4K; confidence intervals absent
Reproducibility concerns: projection head architecture insufficiently detailed, no code availability, batch size 1 stability not discussed, task-specific decoder initialization not specified

strengths: Novel prompt-space conditioning paradigm that addresses a real deployment mismatch in prompt-conditioned models, providing genuine insight beyond prior feature-space adaptation approaches
Comprehensive experimental validation across 4 COD, 5 SOD, and medical imaging benchmarks with rigorous ablations isolating each component and decoupled studies (Table 6) validating core claims
Honest and mechanistic failure analysis (Section G, Fig. 8) clearly characterizing operating boundaries rather than overclaiming robustness
Strong technical design with well-motivated architectural choices (dual-branch SPG, asymmetric PSG gating, continuous logit feeding) supported by empirical validation
Efficient parameter usage (21.26M trainable) and excellent cross-domain generalization to SOD and medical polyp segmentation without task-specific modifications
Superior performance to zero-shot Oracle (0.017 vs. 0.030 MAE on COD10K) and SOTA specialist models while maintaining practical inference speed (29 FPS)
Thorough supplementary material systematically addressing anticipated review risks with quantitative and qualitative evidence
weaknesses: Core failure mode occurs under extreme foreground-background ambiguity—the precise conditions where the method is needed most (Section G shows under-segmentation, truncation, topological fracture); proposed fix (uncertainty-aware generation) mentioned but unimplemented
Severe performance degradation on smaller models: 3-5× MAE increase from SAM2-L to SAM2-T/B (Table 1) with no analysis of root causes, limiting practical deployment on resource-constrained devices
Method tightly coupled to SAM2; applicability to other prompt-conditioned architectures, multi-class segmentation, or video processing (SAM2's key feature) unclear or undiscussed

Insufficient justification of architectural choices: Why TwoWayTransformer for SPG? Why Km=4 tokens? Why specific PSG fusion design? Minimal-SPG ablation uses drastically different architecture, complicating fair comparison
20.7% latency overhead (29 vs. 35 FPS) non-negligible for real-time applications; SPG contributes 9.6% of runtime, potentially prohibitive for edge deployment
Missing quantitative comparisons with recent auto-prompting works [2,36,44] and comprehensive comparison with SAM-based COD methods despite citing them

Generalization tested only on related natural-image foreground-background tasks (COD, SOD, medical polyp); no evaluation on fundamentally different domains, multi-class scenarios, or fine-grained categories
Continuous logit feeding to frozen encoder is unconventional; empirically validated in Table 6 but theoretical justification beyond empirical results lacking

Failure analysis shows negative prompt encroachment on target regions causes catastrophic suppression, revealing potential fundamental limitation of asymmetric gating strategy that may be architecturally irresolvable

strengths: Novel prompt-space conditioning paradigm elegantly addresses the structural mismatch between SAM2's prompt-conditioned design and prompt-absent deployment scenarios, providing principled alternative to feature-space bypassing
State-of-the-art results on 4 COD benchmarks (MAE 0.017 on COD10K, 0.032 on CAMO) with excellent parameter efficiency (21.26M trainable params) and statistical robustness (0.017 ± 0.001)

Exceptionally rigorous experimental validation: Table 3 comprehensively ablates design choices, Table 6 decisively isolates prompt-space conditioning contribution (Minimal-SPG + PromptSpace 0.040 vs. Full-SPG Direct 0.025), all baselines fairly re-trained at identical resolution/data

Exceptional interpretability and transparency: Figure 4 visualizes PSG mechanism with gate decision maps and feature energy changes; Figure 8 provides mechanistic analysis of failure modes via negative prompt encroachment; Appendix H explicitly clarifies operating boundary

Comprehensive generalization evidence: Cross-dataset medical polyp transfer (Table 4), competitive SOD results (Table 5, Appendix A), runtime profiling (Table 7 showing 13.1% overhead in prompt-space modules), cross-seed statistical stability

Non-obvious technical insights (e.g., raw continuous logits outperform binarization; residual anchoring to Z⁺ preserves foreground) validated through systematic ablations (Table 6 II), providing actionable guidance for future prompt-encoder adaptations

Honest limitations discussion acknowledging model capacity dependency, over-suppression failure mode in extreme scenarios, and inability to generalize to multi-instance/semantic segmentation—strengthens scientific contribution through transparency
weaknesses: Evaluation heavily concentrated on camouflaged object detection (extreme foreground-background ambiguity); primary COD experiments dwarf SOD results (relegated to appendix with smaller margins). Applicability to standard segmentation tasks where ambiguity is minimal remains unclear

Severe foundation model dependency: SAM2-T achieves MAE 0.148 on CAMO vs. 0.032 for SAM2-L (4.6× degradation), severely limiting practical applicability in resource-constrained settings. No clear path to address this fundamental limitation

Inherent architectural limitation: Over-suppression failure mode occurs when P⁻ encroaches on weak target regions. While residual anchoring (Z = ψ([Ỹ⁺, φ_feat(Z⁻)]) + Z⁺) provides partial mitigation, this is a band-aid rather than principled solution. Affects non-trivial subset of real-world scenarios

Moderate novelty in component design: SPG is standard transformer decoder with learned queries, PSG is straightforward sigmoid-based gating, LoRA is established PEFT. Novelty concentrated in paradigm framing rather than architectural innovations

Insufficient theoretical justification: Why continuous logits preserve spatial uncertainty better than thresholded masks lacks rigorous explanation. Asymmetric gating optimality asserted rather than formally justified. Interplay between SPG capacity and PSG effectiveness under varying ambiguity levels unexplored

Limited applicability evidence beyond extreme-ambiguity domains: Cross-dataset transfer to medical polyps is single additional domain. No experiments on standard benchmarks (COCO instance, ADE20K semantic) where foreground-background ambiguity is minimal, raising questions about paradigm generality
Computational efficiency trade-offs: 29 FPS with 20.7% overhead over SAM2; SPG contributes 9.6% runtime. While acceptable, real-time applications or edge deployment may find this limiting

Protocol concerns (minor): Empty token baseline represents extremely challenging scenario; real deployment might benefit from noisy/partial prompts. SAM2-AMG top-1 selection via predicted_iou may be suboptimal approximation
